report:
## Research Findings

The claim is **well-supported by strong evidence**, not false.

**Key trial evidence:** The landmark study is Pan CQ et al., published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* (2016), a multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial in China involving pregnant women with chronic hepatitis B and high viral loads (HBV DNA >200,000 IU/mL). Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) was started at 30–32 weeks' gestation. The trial found mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) dropped from about 18% in untreated controls to roughly 5% in the tenofovir group — a highly significant reduction (https://gutsandgrowth.com/2016/08/03/preventing-neonatal-hepatitis-b-transmission-with-tenofovir/; trial PDF at http://www.corevih-bretagne.fr/ckfinder/userfiles/files/Congrès/CROI_2017/Articles_Mercredi_15/Pan+et+al_+-+2016+-+Tenofovir+to+Prevent+Hepatitis+B+Transmission+in+M.pdf).

**Confirmatory evidence:** A subsequent large randomized clinical trial (Pan CQ, Dai E, Mo Z, et al., *JAMA*, 2025) further validated tenofovir's efficacy and safety in preventing HBV MTCT during pregnancy, reinforcing the original findings with additional data (cited via https://www.hepatitisb.uw.edu/go/hbv/preventing-perinatal-transmission-hbv/core-concept/all).

**Meta-analyses and guidelines:** Systematic reviews/meta-analyses confirm antiviral prophylaxis (primarily tenofovir) during late pregnancy meaningfully reduces MTCT when combined with infant immunoprophylaxis (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9812094/). Based on this evidence, the **World Health Organization** formally recommends that HBsAg-positive pregnant women with HBV DNA ≥200,000 IU/mL receive tenofovir prophylaxis starting at 28 weeks' gestation through at least birth (https://www.who.int/teams/global-hiv-hepatitis-and-stis-programmes/hepatitis/prevention/mother-to-child-transmission-of-hepatitis-b).

**Conclusion:** Multiple randomized trials, meta-analyses, and international clinical guidelines converge in support of this intervention. The claim is accurate, and the skepticism is not supported by current evidence.
